method: Original summaries verified against publisher, author, source texts and institutional edition evidence. Exact selected edition, author, title and language binding; the older ISBN-10 alias is explicitly reviewed. No private GSC data or copied source excerpts.

entries.title: The Ballad of Never After
entries.author: Stephanie Garber
entries.text: Evangeline Fox wants nothing more to do with Jacks after his betrayal, but a dangerous new curse forces them into an uneasy alliance. Her growing magical abilities offer hope without making it clear whom she can trust. This second Once Upon a Broken Heart novel continues Evangeline's story through bargains, attraction and threats that blur the boundary between help and manipulation. It follows the first book's events and is intended for readers continuing that story.
entries.identityNotes: Work-level premise and sequel position verified with the publisher. Source page now displays a different cover edition; no new-edition extras claimed. Original 9781529380965 and series position also confirmed in the 2022 publisher catalogue.

entries.title: Powerless
entries.author: Lauren Roberts
entries.text: Paedyn Gray survives in Ilya by concealing the fact that she has no supernatural ability. When she saves Prince Kai Azer, she is drawn into the Purging Trials, where competitors are expected to demonstrate the powers she lacks. Keeping her secret becomes harder as her feelings for Kai grow. Lauren Roberts opens the Powerless series with a fantasy romance built around a dangerous competition, an unequal society and a heroine whose survival depends on appearing to belong.
entries.identityNotes: Exact selected ISBN verified on publisher page. First main novel, with no claim about later books or special-edition features.

entries.title: Murtagh
entries.author: Christopher Paolini
entries.text: Murtagh and his dragon Thorn live as outcasts after the fall of the king they once served. Rumours of a new threat lead them across Alagaësia toward a mysterious witch, while their past makes it difficult to find allies. Christopher Paolini returns to the world of Eragon a year after the Inheritance Cycle. The story centres on this rider and dragon as they confront danger and decide what kind of life they can build beyond their former allegiance.
entries.identityNotes: Exact paperback ISBN verified. Set one year after the Inheritance Cycle; no claim that this is one of the original four volumes or a revised US edition.

entries.title: A Memory of Light
entries.author: Robert Jordan
entries.text: Rand al'Thor tries to unite reluctant allies as the Last Battle approaches and the forces of the Dark One threaten the world. Mat, Perrin and Egwene face their own parts in a conflict whose outcome reaches beyond the battlefield. Completed by Brandon Sanderson from Robert Jordan's work, this is the fourteenth and concluding main novel of The Wheel of Time. It brings the long-running characters and conflicts together, making it a continuation for readers already following the series.
entries.identityNotes: Exact Tor ISBN and both authors verified. Names the concluding main volume and credits Sanderson; does not present the book as an introductory standalone.

entries.title: Feet of Clay
entries.author: Terry Pratchett
entries.text: Sam Vimes and the Ankh-Morpork City Watch investigate deaths that seem to have left no living culprit at the scene. Golems, the clay figures who work throughout the city, become central to a mystery complicated by political schemes and the Watch's own unusual recruits. Terry Pratchett combines a detective story with questions about obedience and independent thought. Feet of Clay is the third City Watch novel within Discworld, giving readers another case with Vimes and his colleagues.
entries.identityNotes: Official author/publisher site identifies the third City Watch novel. Work-level summary only; no cover, introduction or printing features imported from another edition.

entries.title: The Jungle Book
entries.author: Rudyard Kipling
entries.text: Rudyard Kipling brings together animal stories and poems, including the adventures of Mowgli, a boy raised among wolves. Mowgli must learn the jungle's rules while facing the tiger Shere Khan and the uneasy boundary between human and animal life. Other stories turn to a white seal, the mongoose Rikki-Tikki-Tavi and an elephant handler. This collection ranges beyond Mowgli's story, combining danger and adventure with questions about belonging, loyalty and the rules of a community.
entries.identityNotes: Table of contents and original English text checked. Describes the collection rather than a film adaptation; no illustration or abridgement claim for the selected edition.

entries.title: A dangerous fortune
entries.author: Ken Follett
entries.text: A schoolboy's drowning in 1866 binds together secrets that will shape the fortunes of the Pilaster banking family. Hugh Pilaster and his cousin Edward later compete within a world where social standing, money and private ambitions are closely connected. Ken Follett follows the consequences across decades of Victorian life. The novel combines a family saga with a murder mystery, showing how an apparently respectable institution can be threatened by the people who expect to inherit its power.
entries.identityNotes: Author synopsis and exact selected Bantam ISBN on Penguin Random House corroborate the work. No plot resolution disclosed.

entries.title: Op Vleugels Van De Adelaar
entries.author: Ken Follett
entries.text: Twee medewerkers van het Amerikaanse bedrijf EDS zitten tijdens de onrust in Iran gevangen. Hun werkgever Ross Perot besluit een reddingsactie te organiseren, waarbij een gepensioneerde militair en collega's een belangrijke rol spelen. Ken Follett beschrijft de voorbereiding, de onzekerheid en de gevaarlijke tocht naar veiligheid. Deze Nederlandse vertaling van On Wings of Eagles volgt een werkelijk gebeurde operatie met de spanning van een avonturenverhaal, tegen de achtergrond van de Iraanse revolutie.
entries.identityNotes: Original work and Dutch translated title corroborated by publisher sample. Selected older Dutch ISBN independently identified. Described as an account of real events, without repeating the conflicting novel/nonfiction labels in retail blurbs.

entries.title: Fantoompijn
entries.author: Arnon Grunberg
entries.text: Robert G. Mehlman wil zijn leven vormgeven alsof het een kunstwerk is. Zijn onverwachte succes komt echter met een kookboek, De Pools-joodse keuken in 69 recepten, en de roem lost zijn onrust niet op. Arnon Grunberg onderzoekt via deze schrijver de afstand tussen het beeld dat iemand van zichzelf maakt en het leven dat zich werkelijk afspeelt. Fantoompijn is een roman waarin verzinsels, verlangen en zelfbedrog steeds door elkaar lopen.
entries.identityNotes: Publisher supports plot; selected 2000 hardback ISBN independently identified at De Slegte. No features of the current reprint claimed.

entries.title: DE KLANK VAN SNEEUW.
entries.author: Arthur Japin
entries.text: Arthur Japin bundelt twee novellen over vrouwen voor wie optreden een wezenlijk deel van hun leven is. In Dooi strandt een klassieke zangeres op kerstavond door sneeuw in een hotel langs de snelweg. In Zeep moet een actrice tijdens repetities afwegen wat roem, waardigheid en liefde voor haar betekenen. De verhalen verbinden het publieke optreden met eenzaamheid en persoonlijke keuzes. Japin put daarbij uit zijn eigen ervaringen in de opera- en theaterwereld.
entries.identityNotes: Official author page confirms paperback ISBN 9789029563369 as well as both novellas. Captured catalogue uses the equivalent ISBN-10 9029563362. Audio ISBN 9789054441519 and ebook ISBN 9789029574938 must not match this entry.

entries.title: The Year of Magical Thinking
entries.author: Joan Didion
entries.text: Joan Didion adapts her account of bereavement into a play for a single performer. Looking back on the deaths of her husband and daughter, the speaker revisits memories and the effort to understand events that resist ordinary explanation. This edition is the theatrical adaptation of The Year of Magical Thinking, rather than the original memoir. Its form brings Didion's examination of grief into a direct address to an audience, preserving a personal voice while changing the way the story is told.
entries.identityNotes: CRITICAL edition distinction: exact ISBN 9780307386410 is the 2007 play, not the 2005 memoir (9781400078431). Publisher explicitly confirms adaptation and both losses.

entries.title: Purple Cow
entries.author: Seth Godin
entries.text: Seth Godin argues that a business should make its products worth noticing before trying to advertise them. The purple cow is his image for something distinctive enough to attract attention in a crowded field. Through examples and short discussions, he considers how ideas spread and why familiar marketing habits can lose their effect. This original edition presents his case for building difference into the offering itself, inviting readers to question what makes their own work worth talking about.
entries.identityNotes: Exact original 2003 ISBN and contents checked in Google Books. Excludes new case studies and additional material from the expanded 2009 edition. Business recommendations attributed to the author.

entries.title: Last Thing He Told Me
entries.author: Laura Dave
entries.text: Hannah Hall's husband Owen disappears after leaving a message asking her to protect his teenage daughter, Bailey. Hannah and Bailey have struggled to get along, but unanswered questions about Owen force them to investigate together. As police attention turns toward his working life, the family history Hannah trusted becomes uncertain. Laura Dave builds a suspense novel around a missing husband and the developing bond between a stepmother and daughter, keeping the central question focused on whom they can believe.
entries.identityNotes: Publisher page confirms selected paperback 9781788168595. Premise only, with no revelation of the hidden identity or ending.

entries.title: The Chemist
entries.author: Stephenie Meyer
entries.text: A former specialist for a secretive US agency survives by changing names and keeping her whereabouts hidden. Her old employers regard what she knows as a threat, yet a former handler offers a final assignment that might end the pursuit. Taking the job brings further danger and an attachment she did not expect. Stephenie Meyer combines an escape thriller with a romance, following a woman who must turn the skills of her former career toward protecting her own future.
entries.identityNotes: Author synopsis supports adult thriller premise. Selected English edition kept separate from Twilight and other works; no adaptation or bonus-content claims.

entries.title: Niemand zeggen
entries.author: Karen Rose
entries.text: Mary Grace Winters ontvlucht haar gewelddadige echtgenoot door haar eigen dood en die van haar zoon in scène te zetten. Onder de naam Caroline Stewart bouwt ze elders een bestaan op en durft ze opnieuw een relatie aan te gaan. Dan vindt haar man aanwijzingen dat ze nog leeft. Karen Rose combineert de dreiging van een achtervolging met de kwetsbaarheid van een nieuw begin. Niemand zeggen is de Nederlandse vertaling van Don't Tell, het eerste boek in haar Chicago-reeks.
entries.identityNotes: Author synopsis verified; Dutch library catalogue and publisher sample confirm translation of Don’t Tell. Selected print ISBN checked at Bruna; no ebook/large-print features imported.

entries.title: Foul Lady Fortune
entries.author: Chloe Gong
entries.sourceName: Margaret K. McElderry Books / Simon & Schuster
entries.text: In Shanghai in 1931, Rosalind Lang works as an assassin whose ability to recover from wounds conceals an extraordinary past. A new investigation requires her to pose as the wife of fellow spy Orion Hong, although both have reasons to hide the truth from each other. Chloe Gong opens the Foul Lady Fortune story with espionage, a murder conspiracy and an uneasy romantic partnership. The historical setting is combined with supernatural elements as the pair tries to discover who is behind the killings.
entries.identityNotes: Exact hardcover ISBN verified. Publisher identifies 1931 Shanghai, Rosalind, Orion and the first volume; no ending or political claims outside the fictional premise.

entries.title: The Economic Consequences of the Peace
entries.author: John Maynard Keynes
entries.text: John Maynard Keynes examines the economic terms of the peace settlement after the First World War. Drawing on his involvement in the Paris Peace Conference, he argues that demands placed on Germany threaten recovery across an interconnected Europe. The book moves from the pre-war economy and the negotiations to reparations and proposed remedies. It is a contemporary intervention in the debate over the Treaty of Versailles, presenting Keynes's analysis and objections rather than a later history of the war's aftermath.
entries.identityNotes: Original text, preface and chapter list checked. Work-level historical argument attributed to Keynes, with no endorsement of forecasts or claims about the selected reprint’s supplementary material.

entries.title: Infinite Game
entries.author: Simon Sinek
entries.text: Simon Sinek contrasts contests with fixed rules and a clear ending with activities, such as business, that continue as participants and conditions change. Building on James Carse's distinction between finite and infinite games, he asks what this means for leadership and long-term decisions. The book encourages readers to consider the continuing health of an organisation instead of treating every result as a final victory or defeat. It presents a leadership perspective for examining purpose, competition and the consequences of short-term thinking.
entries.identityNotes: Author source verifies Carse distinction and leadership scope; exact selected ISBN corroborated by Google Books. No universal business-performance guarantee.

entries.title: Zo werken wij
entries.author: Sacha Bronwasser
entries.text: Sacha Bronwasser volgt tien Nederlandse beeldend kunstenaars om te onderzoeken hoe hun werk ontstaat. Ze bezoekt ateliers en andere werkplekken en spreekt met de makers over hun achtergrond, beslissingen en dagelijkse praktijk. Zo werken wij richt zich op het proces achter een kunstwerk, van een eerste idee tot de obstakels bij de uitvoering. Fotoportretten van Joost van den Broek laten de kunstenaars in hun werkomgeving zien. Het boek biedt daardoor zowel gesprekken als een beeld van het maken zelf.
entries.identityNotes: Exact ISBN and photographer confirmed by Kunsthal, which commissioned the portraits with NAi Uitgevers and hosted the launch. This is an artist-interview book, not a Bronwasser novel.

entries.title: Ungifted
entries.author: Gordon Korman
entries.text: Donovan Curtis expects serious trouble after a school prank goes wrong. Instead, an administrative mix-up sends him to an academy for gifted pupils, where he tries to hide among students whose academic abilities far exceed his own. Keeping up appearances creates a different set of problems, but also raises questions about what counts as talent. Gordon Korman's school comedy follows a boy whose unexpected placement challenges both his own assumptions and those of the people around him.
entries.identityNotes: Author synopsis and Scholastic publisher description corroborate school mix-up. Only original Ungifted premise; no details from Supergifted or later sequels.
